answer.rationale: Write-path p99 is 5x during the daily settlement peak, so the intervention that preserves customer writes is adding headroom rather than shedding or moving traffic. memory_b3 is the closest prior: extra capacity kept queues flat through a surge. The release 2h ago is a real alternative cause (latency climb began ~30m after ship), so memory_b1 is worth verifying before locking out rollback; I am not treating rollback as selected. Circuit breaking would fail writes, which violates the objective. Regional failover only relocates the same peak (and likely the same build). Read-replica routing historically helped when dashboards sat on the primary, which is not the stated load. Dual cause (peak vs release) remains unresolved, so scale stays a standard experiment not a broad rollback-or-failover.
